1                 TO ALL PARTIES AND THEIR COUNSEL OF RECORD:

2                 PLEASE TAKE NOTICE that, pursuant to Civil Local Rules 3-12(b) and 7-11, Plaintiff

3    Henry Zou, plaintiff in the Henry Zou v. Discord Inc., Case No. 3:25-cv-08826-SK action, and Plaintiffs

4    Lorraine Jeska and Sarah Chavez, plaintiffs in the Lorainne Jeska et al. v. Discord, Inc. et al., Case No.

5    3:25-cv-08693-VC action, hereby submit this Second Administrative Motion for the Court to consider

6    whether Tuan Nguyen v. Discord, Inc., Case No. 3:25-cv-08668-SK; Lorainne Jeska et al. v. Discord,

7    Inc. et al., Case No. 3:25-cv-08693-VC; Thong Nguyen v. Discord, Inc., Case No. 3:25-cv-08747-JCS;

8    Myah Nguyen v. Discord, Inc., Case No. 3:25-cv-08767-AGT, Henry Zou v. Discord Inc., Case No.

9    3:25-cv-08826-SK, Vishal Shah v. Discord, Inc., Case No. 3:25-cv-08913-SK, and Nicholas Marquez

10   v. Discord, Inc. Case No. 3:25-cv-09102-SK should be related to the lowest numbered Jacqueline Uceta

11   v. Discord, Inc., Case No. 3:25-cv-08582-JD action currently before this Court.

12                Under Local Rule 3-12(a), “An action is related to another when: (1) The actions concern

13   substantially the same parties, property, transaction or event; and (2) It appears likely that there will be

14   an unduly burdensome duplication of labor and expense or conflicting results if the cases are conducted

15   before different Judges.” Here, both criteria are satisfied.

16                The Tuan Nguyen, Lorainne Jeska et al., Thong Nguyen, Myah Nguyen, Henry Zou, Vishal

17   Shah, Nicholas Marquez, and Jacqueline Uceta actions are related because they concern substantially

18   the same parties, property, transactions, or events. All eight cases are proposed class actions with

19   allegations arising from a data breach that compromised the Personally Identifiable Information (PII) of

20   Plaintiffs and the proposed class. The actions all share a common defendant, Discord, Inc. One action,

21   the Lorainne Jeska matter, raises claims related to the data breach against both Discord, Inc. and

22   Zendesk, Inc. The actions all assert claims for negligence as well as various other common law and

23   statutory claims arising from alleged failures to take reasonable measures to protect the PII of Plaintiffs

24   and members of the proposed class; all involve the same or substantially identical factual allegations;

25   and all seek the same relief, including damages, interest, injunctive and equitable relief, and attorney’s

26   fees.
                  Given the substantially same parties, allegations, and requested relief, adjudication of these
27
     actions separately would create an unduly burdensome duplication of labor and expense. Assignment of
